'''''Dimorphotheca pluvialis''''', common names '''white African daisy''', '''Cape marigold''', '''weather prophet''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=DIPL4|taxon=Dimorphotheca pluvialis|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> '''Cape rain-daisy''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''ox-eye daisy''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Dimorphotheca pluvialis|url = http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantcd/dimorthothecapluvialis.htm|website = www.plantzafrica.com|access-date = 2016-02-19}}</ref> '''Cape daisy'''<ref name=":0" /> or '''rain daisy''',<ref name=":0" /> is a plant species native to [[South Africa]] and [[Namibia]].<ref name=":0" /> It is sparingly naturalized in scattered locations in [[California]].<ref name="asdfkh8hbuk">{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220004140|title=Dimorphotheca pluvialis in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|accessdate=May 7, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Dimorphotheca%20pluvialis.png|title=Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map|accessdate=May 7, 2023}}</ref>

''Dimorphotheca pluvialis'' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] herb up to 40 cm (16 in) tall. It has long, narrow leaves, sometimes [[Entire leaf|entire]] but sometimes [[Leaf shape|toothed]] or [[pinnate]]ly [[Leaf shape|lobed]]. [[Ray flower]]s are white to yellowish, sometimes with blue or purple markings. [[Disc flower]]s are usually white to yellowish with purple tips.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="asdfkh8hbuk"/><ref>Moench, Conrad. Methodus Plantas Horti Botanici et Agri Marburgensis : a staminum situ describendi 585. 1794.</ref><ref name="tina">{{Cite web|url=http://pza.sanbi.org/dimorphotheca-pluvialis|title=Dimorphotheca pluvialis | PlantZAfrica|website=pza.sanbi.org|accessdate=May 7, 2023}}</ref>
